known.title: Keep the push base out of pull request test runs
Disputed keep 13: Another workflow can clear Forge's failed run
Recheck recent results after scanning pending commits
Gate: Give an actionable next step when the red wait ends
Follow-up: Keep waiting for the planned 90 minutes

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A developer pushes a second commit to an open pull request. GitHub's [synchronize payload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/octokit/webhooks/main/payload-schemas/api.github.com/pull_request/synchronize.schema.json) also contains `before`, so this sets `FORGE_PUSH_BASE` for that pull request run. `fasttest.py:356-366` then compares against the previous pull request head instead of the default branch. For example, a failing test related to a change in the first commit can be omitted after an unrelated second commit, allowing the required check to pass. The same unconditional expression is asserted by `tests/test_merge_waits_while_default_is_red.py:49`.
findings.title: Keep the push base out of pull request test runs

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo has another GitHub Actions workflow with a job named `tests` on the default branch. If Forge's post-merge `tests` fails and that other job succeeds later on the same commit, this filter treats the other job as Forge's newer green result and permits merges. The app slug identifies GitHub Actions, not the workflow, and the code does not check which workflow produced the job. This is distinct from the accepted decision to ignore custom `build` checks: here a custom check masks a failed Forge result.
findings.title: Disputed keep 13: Another workflow can clear Forge's failed run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A busy queue has several recent default-branch commits whose tests are still running. The scan reads a pending run on the newest commit, then makes two sequential GitHub requests per older commit while looking for a finished result. If that already-read run fails during the scan, an older green result still makes `red()` return false, and `merge.py:215-225` proceeds without reading the newer result again. With several pending commits, this window includes multiple network requests and can last seconds, so Forge can merge while the newest finished result is red.
findings.title: Recheck recent results after scanning pending commits

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - The default branch remains red until the wait expires. The refusal's only next step is to rerun `forge merge`, which waits and refuses again while the failure remains. The documented repair requires a fix, an owner merge and a full run; `fullrun.py:14-20` already provides the appropriate full-run command. The refusal must direct the user toward that repair so it names a next action that can resolve the stop.
findings.title: Gate: Give an actionable next step when the red wait ends

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A failed default-branch test is rerun successfully on the same commit while a merge waits. The cases cover pending, cancelled and skipped reruns, a green full-run status already present, and a green result on a new repair commit, but never a later successful `tests` rerun on the failed commit. An implementation that keeps the earlier failed check authoritative over a later successful rerun would pass these cases. The laptop test at line 416 also checks static failure and success, rather than a full run turning green while waiting.
findings.title: Gate: test_3_merge_waits_while_the_default_branch_is_red

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 2
Case: normal use - Reviewing a repair, having the owner merge it and completing its tests takes more than ten minutes. This deadline ends the waiting merge after 600 seconds, although the builder guidance specifies a 90-minute red wait. A green repair arriving later cannot resume that waiting command, so it must be started again.
findings.title: Follow-up: Keep waiting for the planned 90 minutes
